thread:
ingrid: FYI us-west1 GPU attach latency spiked ~03:15. Pods stuck Pending with `attach` errors; attach durations jumped from ~8s to 90s+.
sam: noticed on a couple canaries. Controller logs show `device busy` and a ton of blocked `fsync` calls. Any janitor activity? :thinking_face:
alex: pulling iostat - several scratch NVMe hitting sustained 200-260k IOPS, qdepth saturated on hotstripe nodes.
maya: janitor kicked a deep-scrub sweep across the shard group at 03:12. That tends to create fsync churn when simultaneous with many mounts.
raj: short-term: reduce janitor concurrency or move GPU attaches off nodes with scrub activity. Longer term: add io-aware attach scheduling.
ingrid: relevant attach + kernel tail:
```
[03:16:58] nvme0: completing abort cmd due to internal timeout
[03:17:01] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 987654
k8s: attach-controller: device busy, backing off attach vol-xyz789
```
alex: also seeing SMART reassign counts rising on a few drives; latency spikes correlate with background scrub windows.
maya: propose quick canary: drop SCRUB_CONCURRENCY from 6 -> 1 in canary deployment to see effect.
sam: also patch attach preference to avoid nodes with `io_health=degraded` for next 30m if possible.
ingrid: applying canary env patch:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/janitor SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=1 --record
```
sre-bot: Created incident INC-7894, assigned to @oncall-marc. :rotating_light:
oncall-marc: Im on it. If concurrency drop helps, we can extend throttle and schedule a node health sweep.
raj: note cost alternative: burst these GPU jobs to Dedicated to avoid local NVMe contention, but that costs committed capacity.
alex: for nodes with repeated SMART growth, recommend marking drain=true and reprovision from spare pool. Example drain command:
```
./node-admin drain --node gnode-042 --reason "nvme-reassigns"
```
ingrid: canary applied. Monitoring attach latency and attach success rate; will update in 10m. :eyes:
sam: if latency improves, roll out concurrency=1 across cluster for the 6h maintenance window and run deeper wear analysis overnight.
ingrid: agree. Also pausing large checkpoint/backup jobs for 6h to avoid re-triggering churn. Update incident with mitigation steps.
